objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to produce connected speech by linking words across boundaries (vowel-to-consonant, silent consonant, and /j/ linking) in the context of evaluating their own pronunciation against the PET speaking scale.
materials:
- Headway Pre-Intermediate Pronunciation, p.8
- Worksheet: linked phrases (Greek_alphabet, modern_email, new_idea, computer_information, 14th-century_English, message_in_a_bottle, etc.)
- Audio: Coursebook tracks T1.8, T1.9, T1.10
- Audio: Student recordings (Ana #11111, Gunner #22222, Nine #33333)
- PET pronunciation scale images (EOI entrance exam + final exit exam)

stages.stage: Lead-in — Introducing the PET pronunciation scale
stages.stage_aim: To familiarise learners with the PET speaking assessment criteria by displaying both the entrance and exit exam scales side by side
stages.procedure:
- Display the two PET pronunciation scale images side by side (EOI entrance exam on the left, final exit exam on the right).
- Elicit from Ss: 'What's the difference between these two levels? What do examiners listen for?'
- Highlight key criteria: intelligibility, rhythm, individual sounds, connected speech features.
- Frame the lesson: 'Today we're going to listen to some students and decide where they sit on this scale — then learn one feature that will help you move up.'

stages.stage: Test 1 — Diagnostic ranking of student recordings
stages.stage_aim: To diagnose learners' awareness of pronunciation features by having them evaluate three peer recordings against the PET scale
stages.procedure:
- Explain that Ss will hear three students (Ana, Gunner, Nine) describing a picture.
- Play Ana's recording (#11111). After listening, ask: 'Where on the scale? What features did you notice?' Elicit observations. 3 min.
- Play Gunner's recording (#22222). Ask the same questions. 3 min.
- Play Nine's recording (#33333). Ask the same questions. 3 min.
- Discuss as a class: 'Who scored highest? What did they do differently?' Note that linked speech is one feature that distinguishes higher bands.
- Teacher notes which features Ss notice spontaneously and which they miss — this shapes the Teach stage.

stages.stage: Teach — Clarifying linking patterns with auto-animate
stages.stage_aim: To draw learners' attention to three types of linking (consonant-to-vowel, silent consonant, /j/ linking) and model how they create natural connected speech
stages.procedure:
- Use auto-animate slides to reveal linking step by step. Start with the phrases from the worksheet: Greek_alphabet → modern_email.
- Slide 1 (entry): show 'Greek_alphabet' and 'modern_email' with plain text. Click → Slide 2 (auto-animate reveal): underline the link points between words.
- Elicit the rule: 'When a word ends with a consonant sound and the next begins with a vowel, they link.'
- Move to silent consonant linking: new_idea (/w/), computer_information (/r/). Use auto-animate to show the inserted sound.
- Move to /j/ linking: 14th-century_English. Show how the letter 'y' becomes /j/ before a vowel.
- Drill each phrase chorally and individually after revealing each pattern.

stages.stage_aim: To give learners structured practice applying linking rules by working through every exercise in the worksheet in order
stages.procedure:
- Distribute the worksheet. Work through each exercise in sequence:
  - Exercise 3 (T1.8): Play the track. Ss listen and practise the three illustrated phrases (new_idea, computer_information, 14th-century_English). Drill chorally and individually. 3 min.
  - Exercise 4 (T1.9): Play the track. Ss listen and practise all five phrases from the rules section (Greek_alphabet, modern_email, new_idea, computer_information, 14th-century_English) starting from the end (back-chaining technique). 3 min.
  - Exercise 5: Ss work individually to mark the links in the six phrases (a message_in_a bottle, anger_and_other_emotions, a lot_of_information, How_is_it possible?, quickly_and_easily, words_on_a page). 3 min.
  - T1.10: Play the track. Ss listen and check their link-marking against the audio. Refer to p56 for written answers. 2 min.
  - Exercise 6: Play T1.10 again. Ss listen and practise saying all six phrases with correct linking. 3 min.
- Circulate throughout, providing individual pronunciation feedback.

stages.stage: Individual reading — choosing a phrase to read aloud
stages.stage_aim: To give each student personalised feedback on their connected speech production by reading a self-selected phrase aloud
stages.procedure:
- Tell Ss to choose one phrase from the worksheet that they want to read aloud.
- Give Ss 1-2 minutes to practise silently or with a partner.
- Teacher calls Ss individually (or in small groups) to read their chosen phrase aloud.
- Provide individual feedback on their linking: which links they made correctly, which they missed, and one thing to improve.
- While waiting, other Ss continue practising other phrases from the worksheet with a partner.
